title: Slab-built desk organiser with sections
subtitle: A three-compartment clay tray for pens, scissors, and clips on a desk
excerpt: A desk organiser is a rectangular slab base with two internal divider walls creating three compartments. Built from air-dry clay slabs, it holds its shape without a kiln. Finished exterior is 22 cm x 12 cm with compartments sized for tall pens, short pens, and small items.
sourceNotes: Slab construction derived from first principles.

glossaryTerms.definition: A flat sheet of clay rolled to an even thickness; the building unit for box, tray, and tile construction
Roughening both clay surfaces and applying diluted clay before joining for a strong bond
The stage at which clay holds its shape but remains workable; the best time to add divider walls

content.text: A three-compartment desk tray is a practical slab project that uses the same skills as a basic clay box: rolling an even
slab
, cutting to size, joining wall strips on a flat base. The two internal dividers are added at
leather-hard
stage. Once sealed, the tray is robust enough for daily desk use.

materials.name: Clay slip (same clay thinned with water)
PVA varnish (50/50 with water, for sealing)

content.text: Layout before rolling

The exterior footprint is 22 cm x 12 cm. Two internal dividers create: one deep pen compartment (8 cm wide x 12 cm x 10 cm tall), one medium compartment for scissors (8 cm wide x 12 cm x 7 cm tall), and one shallow tray for clips and erasers (6 cm wide x 12 cm x 4 cm tall). Divider and outer wall heights determine compartment depth. Cut each piece before joining.
Rolling and cutting the pieces
Roll a slab 6 mm thick. Cut the base: 22 cm x 12 cm. Set aside.

From the same slab, cut the outer walls: two long walls (22 cm x 10 cm) and two short end walls (12 cm x 10 cm). These are all 10 cm tall , the compartment heights come from the internal dividers, not the outer walls.

Cut the two internal dividers: both 12 cm x [height]cm matching the compartment heights. First divider: 10 cm tall (between pen compartment and scissors compartment). Second divider: 7 cm tall (between scissors compartment and clip tray).
Assembling the outer box
Allow the base and wall pieces to stiffen for 30 minutes so they hold shape during assembly.
Use the
Score-and-slip
each wall to the base perimeter one wall at a time. Stand each wall upright, press firmly, and blend the interior corner with a damp wooden rib.
Allow the box to firm for one hour before adding the dividers.
Adding the dividers

Measure and mark the divider positions on the base and side walls. Score the base and walls at each mark. Apply slip. Press the first divider into place and blend both sides of the divider-to-base join and the divider-to-end-wall joins. Repeat for the second divider.
Drying and sealing

Dry the organiser upright on a flat board, covering loosely with a cloth for the first 24 hours. The air-dry clay shrinks as it dries; check that dividers have not pulled away from the walls. Blend any small gaps at leather-hard. Once fully bone-dry, apply two coats of diluted PVA to all surfaces.
Variations
Add a small circular pen holder (coil-built cylinder) to the back of the base as a fourth compartment.
Press a stamp pattern along the outer walls before drying for surface texture.
Paint with acrylic and seal with a gloss coat for a smooth finished look.
Troubleshooter

items.problem: Divider cracked at the base join
items.cause: Added when the outer box was too dry for slip to bond, or the join was not blended on both sides
items.fix: At leather-hard, rework with fresh slip and a wooden rib. For bone-dry cracks, fill with PVA

items.problem: Box walls bowed outward on drying
items.cause: Outer walls too tall and thin without internal bracing
items.fix: Add the dividers before the walls have a chance to bow. A thin card support inside each compartment during drying can also prevent bowing
